neighbours.label: The word 'other' before people or people's possessions and experiences.
fire: He keeps spending other people's savings on risky ventures.
She listened carefully to other people's stories.
The comedian laughs at other people's mistakes.
Please respect other people's privacy in the waiting room.
He takes credit for other people's work in the office.
The game lets us explore other people's memories.
She worries about other people's opinions of her painting.
The guide explains how to understand other people's feelings.
quiet: He keeps spending his own savings on risky ventures.
She listened carefully to her family's stories.
The comedian laughs at his own mistakes.
Please respect each person's privacy in the waiting room.
He takes credit for his colleagues' work in the office.
The game lets us explore our own memories.
She worries about her friends' opinions of her painting.
The guide explains how to understand your neighbors' feelings.

predictions: Fire sentences should outrank the matched near misses; assessed once by quick-8+8@2. Failure is retained without revision.
notes: Random 16-pole sweep. Labels derived from both-pole cards and top-32 peak-token counts. No band archive covers this neuron. Sentences authored by Codex; no Bonsai-generated sentences. Exploratory probes, when declared, used different sentences from this pre-registration.
